scene: a handwritten card taped inside the glass door of a small bakery, biro on the back of a receipt roll, the word CLOSED and a date and the word sorry underlined once, the tape gone amber at its corners, an empty wooden shelf and a wire basket behind the glass, the photographer's own reflection cropped to a shoulder and a hand, flat overcast light from the street

a fibre egg tray on a market trestle, twenty-nine eggs of unmatched sizes and four different browns, one with a feather still stuck to it, a hand-lettered price card leaning against the tray, a crate of tomatoes going soft at the edge of frame, morning sun coming in low and hard across the table under a canvas awning

the round pressure gauge of a wall boiler in a hall cupboard, the needle sitting below the green band, condensation inside the glass, a copper filling loop and a seized grey lever underneath, a coat sleeve and the edge of a hoover in the dark behind, the whole thing lit by a phone torch from one side

a dark sourdough loaf on a chopping board at night, one end already cut and eaten standing up, crumbs everywhere, the crust blistered and floured, a kitchen knife laid across the board and a mug behind it, the only light a warm bulb directly overhead throwing a hard shadow off the loaf

a heavy pan of white bean and fennel soup seen from above on a gas hob, the surface still moving, a wooden spoon resting across the rim, fennel fronds and a dried chilli on the counter beside it, the hob steel scratched and clean, daylight from a window to the left

a school art room in the holidays, chairs upside down on the tables, blinds down and edged with hard white light, the display boards stripped back to bare cork with staples still in them, a trolley of empty trays against the wall, one tall stool missing from a row of four, the floor swept and dull

the button panel of an old lift photographed close, the numbers worn to ghosts on brushed steel, the alarm bell symbol scratched around from years of pressing, a stop button with its red gone pink, the panel's screws not quite aligned, the mirrored back wall of the car doubling the picture behind, tube light from above

a sketchbook open on a kitchen table to four attempts at the same lift panel, the first two in pencil and the last two in biro, the mirror worked over and over until the paper has gone grey and furred, a note to herself in the margin, the page cockled where an eraser has been used hard, warm evening light from one side
